newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SIA sees easier ownership rules.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SIA sees easier ownership rules.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) chief executive officer Cheong Choong Kong said on Tuesday he expected the ownership restictions on air carriers to ease in the future.
At present, limits are usually set on foreign ownership of international airlines, particularly by other airines, Cheong said in a speech to National Aviation Press Club of Australia.
"My prediction is that caps, where they exist, will be removed eventually," said Cheong, who is also deputy chairman of the Singapore carrier.
He said in Australia and the United States the cap is 25 percent, while in Britain and Malaysia there is no cap.
"When that happens, our existing bilateral system will become unworkable," Cheong said.

"If, for example, British Airways owned more than half of Qantas, would it make sense for the British and Australian authorities to continue negotiating air rights on behalf of their airlines?" he said.
British Airways has a 25 percent stake in Qantas, which was privatised by the Australian government last year.
Cheong said in a wide ranging speech that regulators should no longer take account of the special interests of a state-owned monolopy flag carrier when setting aviation policy.
"Other factors, such as national economic and consumer benefits, increasingly come into play," Cheong said.

Cheong said although regulators were slow to accommodate the commercial dynamics of the international aviation industry, more goverments were recognising that less regulation meant better airlines and better service.
